## Fagus sylvatica

_Fagus_ _sylvatica_

Common name:

European Beech

Pronunciation:

FA-gus sil-VAT-i-ka

Family:

Fagaceae

Genus:

[Fagus](https://landscapeplants.oregonstate.edu/fagus)

Type:

Broadleaf

Native to (or naturalized in) Oregon:

No

- Deciduous tree, 50-75 ft (15-23 m) tall and 40-60 ft (12-18 m) spread, pyramidal to oval, dense.  Bark smooth gray, developing an elephant hide appearance on old trunks.  Buds narrow, long (2-2.5 cm), pointed.  Leaves simple, alternate, 5-10 cm long, usually entire (silky and fringed with hairs \[ciliate\] when young), undulate, 5-9 vein pairs ( _F. grandifolia_ has 9-14 pair), acute apex, lustrous dark green above, light green beneath, glabrous at maturity, silky, ciliate when young; petiole 0.5-1 cm long, downy.  Flowers open as leaves are expanding, mal
